name: Data Cleaning Checklist
description: This module is a pre-completion checklist for data cleaning work: a short set of checks to run before calling a data cleaning task done.
content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for data cleaning work: a short set of checks to run before calling a data cleaning task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Document any non-obvious data cleaning decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
2. When data cleaning guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. Re-check edge cases relevant to data cleaning (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
4. Before starting data cleaning work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
5. State assumptions about data cleaning explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
6. Surface known limitations of a chosen data cleaning approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
7. Check that data cleaning terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
8. Validate data cleaning outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting data cleaning assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not apply generic data cleaning advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new data cleaning abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated data cleaning concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of data cleaning correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for data cleaning, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
